To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the rational design of single-site catalysts is a promising strategy to achieve high selectivity in catalytic transformations of bulky and complex molecules”.

single-site heterogeneous catalyst systems can be prepared with a very high degree of control on the nature of the active site and on the chemical surroundings, which is the key factor for the achievement of highly selective catalytic systems.

(1) The design and synthesis of single-site heterogeneous catalytic systems for the selective conversion of bulk molecules is possible; (2) The catalytic properties of the single-site heterogeneous catalyst are determined not only by the active metal site, but also by the support; (3) The catalytic activity, selectivity and stability of the single-site catalysts can be tuned by changing the nature and the structure of the support, as well as by the preparation procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new catalytic systems for the sustainable transformation and upgrading of renewable resources.
the development of new catalytic materials for the selective synthesis of fine chemicals and polymers.
the rational design and preparation of heterogeneous catalysts with single-site active centres, which are able to promote the selective transformation of bulky organic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rational design of single-site catalysts has been proven to be an efficient and successful strategy to achieve high catalytic performance.
the future of single-site heterogeneous catalysis is bright.
the rational design of single-site catalysts is a very powerful tool for achieving highly selective transformations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rational design of single-site catalysts on inorganics is a promising approach to obtain highly efficient catalysts for the production of fine chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and to reduce the environmental impact of chemical processes.
single site catalysis is the future of catalysis.

the combination of the knowledge on the structure and reactivity of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts with the new synthetic methodologies and characterization techniques allows us to design, synthesize and characterize single-site heterogeneous catalyst with enhanced selectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of single-site catalysts is a very challenging but not impossible task.

the control of the chemical environment around the active site, in terms of geometry and chemical nature, is a key factor for the design of single-site catalysts with enhanced chemo- and regioselectivity.

, for the design of single-site catalytic systems, a rational approach is required, which involves the combination of the knowledge of the structure–activity relationship of the active sites with the ability to control the preparation of the active sites at the molecular level.
